pr_title: fix(rust): skip null/empty values if replace_lit_n_char

issue_context.title: `expr.str().replace()` panics on empty string
issue_context.body:
### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://crates.io/crates/polars) of Polars.


### Reproducible example

```rust
fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let df = df!["s" => [""]]
        .unwrap()
        .lazy()
        .with_column(col("s").str().replace(lit(" "), lit("."), true));  // also happens with false

    println!("{:?}", df.collect()?);

    Ok(())
}
```

### Issue description

When using `expr.str().replace(...)` and `expo` is a column containing an empty string, this will panic.

From a quick glance, it looks like it is assumed that below that `offsets_iter` has at least two elements. If the input is empty then I believe it has just one.

https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/58b0da8bc31d71d21be8782c5013747516652f81/crates/polars-ops/src/chunked_array/strings/replace.rs#L47-L51

### Expected behavior

An empty string in the input remains unchanged after replace, and no error.

I think the fix might just be inserting

```rust
if start == end { return arr.clone(); }
```

here:

https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/58b0da8bc31d71d21be8782c5013747516652f81/crates/polars-ops/src/chunked_array/strings/replace.rs#L41-L43


### Installed versions

```toml
polars = { version = "0.36.*", features = ["lazy", "strings", "lazy_regex"] }
```

review_comments: we skip all leading null & empty values, otherwise this will overflow(negative usize).
